primitives.purpose: Billy the Beaver, the Personal Agent mascot. The package exports a conversation portrait, a full-body sprite, registered accessory layers, icon artwork, an optional web greeting animation, and Billy's pixel world: scenery (hills, water, logs, the sun and moon, clouds, sparkles, a night star, a frame) and 16-pixel icons as static SVGs drawn on an 8-pixel grid.

The design tokens of the marketing site and the iOS app: one tokens.json (colors in light and dark, type, spacing, radii, sizes, shadows, and motion) in the Billy design system format. A build writes tokens.css (custom properties with a dark theme and reduced motion) and theme.json (resolved colors and point values for the native app), and refuses any color pair in contrast.pairs that is below its WCAG AA minimum in any theme.

The Cloudflare Worker entry of apps/agent and the Edge. The Edge accepts the Telegram webhook with its secret token, finds the Owner through the Directory, and answers only after the Personal Agent stores the Event. It records a metric for each refused request. It also has the Operator route that adds an Owner. It stores no Owner data.

The Directory in D1 with its Drizzle schema and migrations: Owners, Channel Identities, and the Registration state. Its interface finds the Owner for a Channel Identity, adds an Owner with a Channel Identity, and reads the Registration state. No other module runs SQL against the Directory.

One Durable Object for each Owner, built on the pinned Agents SDK. personalAgentFor finds it by Owner Id. Each object builds one Effect runtime over its SQLite storage. It stores each Event in the Inbox (Owner messages go first in a Turn), keeps the Owner Channel Conversation from the Owner's messages, schedules the Turn with a durable alarm, and runs the Turn: model reply, Journal Entries, and the Channel send. For an Owner message the Turn shows the Acknowledge typing signal (acknowledge) at once and every typingRepeatMillis until the reply or the honest failure notice starts to send, or until a silent Turn ends; a failed typing signal is logged and never fails or delays the Turn, and Reminders, Scheduled Tasks, and Proactive Messages show none. An Owner message Turn answers a Burst (burst): the pending Owner messages that the Turn takes as its input in arrival order. The first Event of the Burst keys the Delivery, the Turn progress, the tools, the Conversation, the Trace, and the metric, and the outcome goes to the newest message. Before the model call an AnsweredByTurn Journal Entry links each other Event to the Turn Event, so recovery after a reset joins a pending Event to its Turn or settles it from the Delivery of that Turn. After a reset, a Turn whose Delivery has started keeps only the Events linked to it, and a pending Event that no Turn linked waits for a new Burst. A linked Burst whose Delivery has not started waits for its Quiet Gap like a new one, so a message that arrived during the reset joins it. An Owner message does not start a Turn at once (burst-wait, decision 0022): the Personal Agent stores it, shows typing once while the Burst waits, and the alarm runs the Turn when burstQuietMillis has passed since the newest pending Owner message, or burstMaxWaitMillis since the first, whichever comes first. The Burst is every pending Owner message in arrival order, and the system prompt says that a later value replaces an earlier one. A Turn restarts when an Owner message arrives mid-Turn (turn-restart, decision 0025, Option A): after the model call and before Delivery, the Turn checks the Inbox for a pending Owner message that arrived after the newest message of its Burst and has no Turn of its own. When there is one, and fewer than burstMaxRestarts restarts were written for the Turn Event, and burstMaxWaitMillis has not passed since the first message, the Turn sends nothing. It writes the restart record (an EventReceived Journal Entry for the Turn Event with a restart field that holds the covered and new Event ids) and a Trace with the restart in one transaction, then an Operator metric with the result superseded, and leaves the Events pending. The next Turn starts after the Quiet Gap with every message of the Burst, including the new one, and the tool calls that already finished come back as completed steps from Turn progress, the same way as after a reset, so a write tool is not called again. A message that arrives after the send gets its own Turn. A skipped or failed Scheduled Task saves its notice to the Conversation, and recovery after a reset restores it with the prompt redacted. When the alarm runs, each due Schedule enters the Inbox as a ScheduleFired Event, and the Turn loop routes each one to the Fired Schedule module (fired-schedule). It reads the Schedule once, checks that it is still due, applies the lateness rule, and then delivers a Reminder by code, with no model call, to the Owner Channel Conversation, or runs the Budget check and a Model Turn for a Scheduled Task. A failed send is recorded and completes the Schedule (decision 0018). It completes the Schedule by the rules of decisions 0013, 0016, 0017, and 0018, and recovers through the Delivery state. The Delivery module (delivery) owns the delivery Journal Entries of a Turn, keyed by its Event, reads their state as a closed union, and writes one Trace and one Operator metric for each Event. Delivery is the one outcome that the agent delivers for a Turn: a reply, a reaction, or silence. An Owner message Turn from the Owner (not a proactive Turn, a Scheduled Task Turn, or a Turn for an untrusted Event) offers the outcome tools stay_silent and react, tools with no execute function that end the tool loop (decisions 0021, 0023, and 0024). Code decides it after the loop (outcome-tools): it refuses silence when the Journal of the Turn Event has an Entry that changed Owner data (a Note, an Open Loop, a Schedule, the Profile, or an Owner Preference) or when a call of a tool that may change Owner data failed, and gives the refusal to the model as the tool result, so the model answers with text within the same step limit. Accepted silence makes no Channel call and writes a StayedSilent Journal Entry, whose Delivery state Silent is final, so recovery after a reset never sends, and the other Events of its Burst are done. Code refuses react only when a changing tool call failed. An accepted reaction is checked with the Channel allowedReaction (an emoji that the Channel does not allow becomes a close match or the Behavior Config defaultReaction) and delivered on the newest Owner message of the Burst as one Delivery: a ReplyPlanned Entry that carries the reaction and its target message, SendStarted, and ReplySent or ReplyFailed. A version without reactions reads that Entry as an empty text plan, so a rollback never blocks recovery. A reaction that Telegram did not confirm (it could not be reached or gave an unreadable answer) is sent once more, in the Turn or by recovery after a reset (ReactionUnconfirmed) to the message that the plan recorded, because setting a reaction is idempotent; a refusal is final. When a Turn that changed Owner data, with no failed changing tool call, ends with no text and no outcome tool call, code reacts with defaultReaction. A failed model call still sends the honest failure text. The Model Turn module (model-turn) runs the reply Turn and the Scheduled Task Turn: the step limit, the model call through the Model Gateway, the Trace, the failure branches, the Conversation write, and the metric. It redacts the saved input and the output once, and sends through Delivery. Each kind of Turn gives it only its Model Task, input, tools, system prompt section, failure notice, late text, and an optional check before the first step. A tool with a side effect saves its call and result in the same transaction as its write, so a Turn that restarts replays them and does not run the tool again. A recorded tool that fails saves its call and the error result after the rolled-back write, so a restarted Turn sees the failure. It writes the conversation of each Event once, and Journal recovery finishes a write that a reset cut off. It owns the Drizzle storage schema and the versioned migrations that each Personal Agent applies once, in order, when it starts. Every Turn adds the Owner's current local date, time, weekday, and time zone (read from the Effect Clock) as the last section of the system prompt, or says that the time zone is not known. A ScheduleFired Event of a Schedule with setBy agent goes to the proactive path (fired-proactive) and not to the Scheduled Task Turn: a Model Turn with the Model Task proactive, the read tools, list_open_loops, and close_open_loop, and the Open Loops in reach in the system prompt. It sends one Proactive Message with no failure notice, and the Schedule completes also when the send fails (decision 0019). The gate (apps/agent/src/proactive/proactive-gate.ts) decides every ScheduleFired Event of a Schedule with setBy agent before any model call, as a closed union: Send, Hold, or FoldIntoBrief. In Quiet Hours the decision is Hold: the Schedule moves to the end of Quiet Hours, a ProactiveMessageHeld Journal Entry records the old and new instant and the reason, a Trace with the result proactive_message_held is written in the same transaction, and no model call happens. A repeated hold of the same Event reuses the journaled instant. When an Owner message arrives, one transaction stores it and connects it to the last sent Proactive Message that has no Outcome and whose response window has not ended. The Turn of a connected message has the Proactive Message and its Open Loops in its system prompt, and when it ends (also after a recovery) code records acted, muted, or replied from the Journal Entries of the Turn. A Turn run and the alarm also record the Outcome of a connected Event that left the Inbox before its Outcome was written. The alarm records ignored for a message with no connected Owner message at the end of its window, with no model call. A proactive Turn sees the recent Outcomes of each Open Loop in reach. The gate result FoldIntoBrief has the reasons muted, message_budget, and token_budget. A follow-up whose open Open Loops are all muted, or that comes when the daily send Budget or proactiveDailyTokenBudget is used up (the Brief always runs), completes with no model call, a ProactiveMessageFolded Journal Entry, and a proactive_message_folded Trace (with the Budget and the used amount for a Budget reason). With no active Brief the Journal Entry is ProactiveMessageSkipped and the Trace result proactive_message_skipped. The Operator metric of the kind proactive_message has the result folded or skipped; the Brief still lists those Open Loops. set_schedule refuses a follow-up for a muted Open Loop. When the gate sends a Proactive Message it merges the other agent Schedules that are due within proactiveMergeWindowMillis (30 minutes) into the same Turn (fired-merge): a ProactiveMessageMerged Journal Entry names them before the model call, the one message counts as one send, and each merged Schedule completes or moves once, also in recovery after a reset. A follow-up that fires while the Brief is due within the window gets FoldIntoBrief with the reason brief_soon.

The Event, a tagged union: OwnerMessage (what a Channel gives to the Personal Agent) and ScheduleFired (a Schedule id and the due instant). The Inbox keeps one ScheduleFired Event for each Schedule id and due instant. The alarm of the Personal Agent creates it for each due Schedule.

The append-only Journal in the Personal Agent SQLite. The interface has append, read, and read for one Event, with no update or delete, and storage triggers refuse updates and deletes. BriefCreated records the creation of the Brief. ProactiveMessageHeld records a hold of a Proactive Message in Quiet Hours. ProactiveMuteChanged records a mute or an undo, ProactiveMessageFolded records a folded follow-up, and ProactiveMessagePlanned orders the Open Loops that a Proactive Message lists against the folds. AnsweredByTurn links an Owner message Event to the Turn Event of the Burst that answers it. TurnSuperseded is not an Entry kind: a Turn that dropped its answer because an Owner message arrived mid-Turn writes an EventReceived Entry for its Turn Event with an optional restart field (the Event ids that the restarted Turn covers and the new ones), so a version without restarts still reads it (decision 0025); the count of these Entries for a Turn Event is its restart count.

The Document primitive (Notes). A Note has a Note id, Owner Id, text, optional URL, source (Event and Channel message), trust level (owner or untrusted), captured date, and last-checked date. It lives in the Personal Agent SQLite. The capture_note tool writes a Note; code sets the source and the trust level from the Event, not the model; an Event with a forward origin gives an untrusted Note whose source holds the forward origin and whose text is the forwarded text, whatever text the model passes, and the tool result shows that text inside the Untrusted Content markers. A Turn for an untrusted Event gets no update_note tool and no update_profile tool. Code escapes the markers inside marked text. A unique constraint on the source Event id and the hash of the normalized text at capture (an edit keeps it) makes a repeated write return the existing Note. Each Note write appends a Journal Entry with the Note id. An FTS5 table over the Note text and URL (versioned migration, triggers keep it in step with the notes table in the same transaction) ranks matches by bm25. A note_links table (from Note, to Note, created date; the pair is stored in id order, so a link is undirected) links related Notes. The capture_note tool takes optional Note ids to link; code rejects an id that is not a Note of the Owner, and the tool returns an error and writes nothing. The update_note tool changes the text or the links of one Note, sets its last-checked date, and appends a NoteUpdated Journal Entry with the Note id and the kind of change (text, links, or text_and_links); the FTS5 table stays in step through its triggers. An update that changes nothing in storage (the same text, links that already exist or are already gone, the same Open Loop) writes no column, no last-checked date, and no Journal Entry, so a repeated call after a reset writes no second change. The search_notes tool takes a query and a limit and returns Note id, text, URL, source, trust level, captured date, last-checked date, and, for each match, its five newest linked Notes (ordered by the date of the link, each with Note id, text, URL, source, trust level, and captured date) and the total count of its links. The list_linked_notes tool takes a Note id and an offset and returns the next five linked Notes of that Note, newest link first, with the total count, so older context stays reachable; text of an untrusted Note is marked as Untrusted Content. The system prompt asks for the source and the date in each answer and for an honest "I do not know" when no Note matches. The agent does not fetch links. A list read returns every Note of the Owner with its linked Note ids, for the Eval runner. An Open Loop is optional metadata on a Note (versioned migration adds the columns open_loop_kind, open_loop_state open or closed, open_loop_closed_reason done, dropped, or replaced, and open_loop_due_at as a UTC instant; check constraints refuse inconsistent columns, and code reads and writes them only through an Effect Schema, as a tagged union Open or Closed). capture_note and update_note take an optional openLoop (a kind and an optional local due time, converted with the Owner time zone; a due time with no known time zone fails with a message and writes nothing). update_note opens an Open Loop on a Note with none or a closed one, and replaces the kind and the due time of an open one. close_open_loop (Note id and reason) closes it; an unknown Note or a Note with no open Open Loop returns an error and writes nothing, and a repeat of the same close in one Event returns the closed Open Loop and writes nothing. Each change appends OpenLoopOpened, OpenLoopChanged (kind and due instant), or OpenLoopClosed (reason) to the Journal in the same transaction; a repeated open or change with the same values writes nothing. list_open_loops returns open Open Loops only, the earliest due first and then the ones with no due date, ten at a time from an offset, with the total count. search_notes, list_linked_notes, and the other note tools show the Open Loop of each Note (kind, state, close reason, due instant, local due time). A Turn for an untrusted Event can keep a Note with an Open Loop and gets list_open_loops, but no update_note or close_open_loop. Existing Notes keep no Open Loop.

The Profile primitive: the short core facts and style rules about the Owner, in the profile_entries table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration). An entry has an entry id, a kind (fact or style_rule), text, the source Event id, and the added date; the same kind and text is stored once. The update_profile tool adds or removes one entry; code, not the model, checks the hard size limit (maxProfileCharacters of the Behavior Config, counted as the characters of all entry texts). An add that would pass the limit writes nothing and returns an error result, and the system prompt tells the agent to tell the Owner. A remove of an unknown entry id returns an error and writes nothing. Every Turn reads the whole Profile and puts it, with the entry ids, in the system prompt, so the Trace holds it. Each change appends a ProfileEntryAdded (entry id and kind) or ProfileEntryRemoved (entry id) Journal Entry, and the tool call is in the Trace. The recall rule of the system prompt answers from the Profile first and searches Notes only when the Profile has no answer.

The Schedule primitive: a wake-up time. The schedules table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration) is the only source of truth. A Schedule has a Schedule id, Owner Id, Action (a Schema tagged union, SendText { text } or RunPrompt { prompt }, stored in the action and text columns and read only through a Schema), set by (owner or agent), optional Note id (a foreign key to the Note; the later Forget slice deletes linked Schedules), next due instant (UTC), state (active, done, cancelled), the source Event id, and created and changed instants. A unique key on the source Event id and the request makes a repeated set_schedule call return the existing Schedule. Each set appends a ScheduleSet Journal Entry, each fire a ScheduleFired entry, and each completion a ScheduleCompleted entry, all with the Schedule id. The set_schedule tool works only for an Event with Trust Level owner. It takes an action, a local due time or a repeat rule, an optional Note id, and optional Open Loop ids (Note ids, at most 20; the link table schedule_open_loops stores them). The action is a tagged union: SendText with its text, or RunPrompt with its prompt, which makes a Scheduled Task. The local due time has the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm. Code converts the local time with the Owner time zone (Effect DateTime makeZoned, disambiguation later), sets set by (agent for a follow-up: a call with Open Loop ids and no ownerAskedForSchedule flag, always in a proactive Turn, where it needs a RunPrompt action and an Open Loop id; otherwise owner), and refuses with a message for the model when the time zone is not known, the time is not real, or the time is in the past. The result gives the local weekday, date, and time. The Schedules store owns the alarm: it keeps one Agents SDK Schedule (callback fireDueSchedules) at the earliest of four instants: the instant when the pending Owner messages are due as a Burst (decision 0022; one minute ahead once that instant has passed and they are still pending), the earliest due instant of the active Schedules that have no Inbox Event yet, one millisecond after the earliest response window end of a sent Proactive Message that has no Outcome and no connected Owner message, and, while a connected Owner message has no Outcome recorded, now when it has left the Inbox and one minute ahead when it is still pending (decision 0019), through the AlarmClock port, arms it again inside each set, change, cancel, completion, and time zone change, and leaves none when no Schedule qualifies. When the alarm fires, the store arms it again only after the ScheduleFired Events are stored and the Turn is queued, so a reset in that gap leaves the alarm to run again. No caller outside the store arms the alarm. A Reminder whose send failed or was not confirmed completes its Schedule (a one-time Reminder becomes done, a repeating one moves to its next occurrence), so the alarm never loops on it. The list_schedules, change_schedule, and cancel_schedule tools work only for an Event with Trust Level owner. They work on every active Schedule, a Reminder or a Scheduled Task. list_schedules gives each Schedule with its id, Action (the text or the prompt), optional Note id, set by, Open Loop ids, and local weekday, date, and time. change_schedule takes a new action, a new local due time or repeat rule, or both. It can change a SendText Schedule into RunPrompt and the opposite. It refuses a time that is not real or is in the past. cancel_schedule sets the state to cancelled. A cancelled Schedule never fires, also when its Event is already in the Inbox. A change or cancel of an unknown, done, or cancelled Schedule changes nothing and returns a message for the model. Each change appends a ScheduleChanged Journal Entry and each cancel a ScheduleCancelled entry, with the Schedule id, in the same transaction as the write, and the store arms the alarm again after each. set_schedule refuses a new RunPrompt Schedule, and change_schedule refuses a change of a SendText Schedule into one, when the Owner has maxActiveScheduledTasks active Scheduled Tasks (an Owner request counts against maxActiveScheduledTasks; an agent follow-up, a RunPrompt Schedule with set by agent, counts against maxActiveAgentSchedules instead). A SendText Schedule is not limited. The Brief (schedule/brief.ts): the first set_time_zone creates one Daily RunPrompt Schedule with setBy agent at the end of the default Quiet Hours and a BriefCreated Journal Entry; later changes create no second one, and a cancelled Brief is not created again. The active limit counts only Schedules that the Owner set. maxActiveAgentSchedules (20) limits active Schedules with set by agent, the Brief included, and is checked after the exactly-once lookup. set_schedule refuses a Note id in openLoopIds that has no open Open Loop; the standalone noteId may still name any owned Note. A proactive Turn has set_schedule; a Turn for an untrusted Event has none. The Schedules store moves a due instant in two cases that code owns: a time zone change moves repeating Schedules, and a hold moves a Schedule of the agent to the end of Quiet Hours.

The Owner Preferences primitive and the time of the Owner. Typed preferences live in the owner_preferences table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration), each checked by a Schema on write and read. The first preference is the time zone, an IANA name that DateTime.zoneMakeNamed accepts. The Owner Preference overrides the Behavior Config default. Each change appends an OwnerPreferenceChanged Journal Entry. The set_time_zone tool (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) sets it and returns a message for the model, with no change, for an invalid name. The time module renders the current local date, time, weekday, and time zone of the Owner from the Effect Clock. Each stored value records its source (owner now; later a Profile or an integration) in a text column with no check on its values, so a new source needs no schema change. The second preference is quiet_hours, the local start and end as HH:mm with a start that differs from the end. With no stored value, the Behavior Config default applies. The quiet_hours tool (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) reads or changes it, and moves a Brief that was at the old end of Quiet Hours to the new end. The pure function endOfQuietHours (time module) returns the end of Quiet Hours when an instant is inside them, across midnight and across a daylight saving change. The preference proactive_message_budget is a whole number from 0 to 24 of Proactive Messages per local day, with the Behavior Config default 3 and the same source rule. The proactive_message_budget tool (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) reads or changes it. The gate counts the Proactive Messages with a sent instant in the local day of the Owner against it. The third preference is muted_proactive_messages, the Open Loop ids and the normalized kinds that the Owner asked for less of. The mute_proactive_message tool (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) mutes, undoes, and lists it, and appends a ProactiveMuteChanged Journal Entry.

The one interface to models. It selects the model for a Model Task. Each Model Task has its own route of model and thinking level. The Model Tasks are reply, scheduled_task, and eval_judge (for the Eval judge). The scheduled_task route is the reply route by default. The Gateway also resolves the Model Credentials (token and billing mode). It calls the model with the AI SDK through Cloudflare AI Gateway, with the Owner Id as metadata and no stored bodies. It retries with a timeout for each try. It records Usage for each model call in the Personal Agent SQLite, with the time from the Effect clock. The Usage ledger sums the input and output tokens of one Model Task since an instant. The daily Token Budget of Scheduled Tasks reads that sum. The Model Task proactive has its own route and Usage rows.

The module that wraps every agent tool. A tool gives its name, its input schema, its work, and its failure message. The module marks the model step, records the tool call and its result in the same transaction as the work with redaction, and keeps a ToolFailed from the work and maps any other failure to ToolFailed with the failure message. It records the decoded input, or the result of an optional recordedInput function of the tool (capture_note uses it to keep the Untrusted Content marking of forwarded text). agentToolServices collects the services that the tools of both kinds of Turn need. Approval and Auto-review plug in here later.

The Trace and the Operator metrics of a Turn. The Trace is one append-only record for each model-answered Event. A Scheduled Task Turn is a model-answered Event, and its record also has the Schedule id and the due instant. A skipped Scheduled Task has a record with the Schedule id, the due instant, the Budget, the spent tokens, and the message. It has no model fields. A Reminder delivery has a record with the Schedule id, the due instant, the text, and the result, and no model fields. The records are in the Personal Agent SQLite. A model-answered record has the system prompt, the messages, the model settings, tool calls, the reply or the error, Usage, and latency. That is enough to replay the Turn, and it holds private content, so it stays with the Owner. The Operator metrics are one Analytics Engine data point for each Turn, Reminder, skipped Scheduled Task, and refused request. A data point for an Event has the Event id as its fifth blob. A reply Turn, Scheduled Task Turn, or proactive Turn records its outcome (reply, silent, or reaction with its emoji and the requested emoji when code replaced it, or null when the model failed) and the refused outcome tools in its Trace, and a turn data point has the outcome kind as its sixth blob, the result silent for a silent Turn, and the result reacted for a delivered reaction. A turn data point has the restart count of its Turn Event as its eighth double, and a Turn that restarts writes a data point with the result superseded for each dropped answer, with the same Event id as the final one. A Trace of a dropped answer has a restart field with the covered and new Event ids. A reset can repeat a data point, so readers count distinct Event ids. A data point has the Owner Id (or none), result, latency, tokens, cost, and cache hits, and no content. The Redactor removes secret values from error text before it enters a Trace or the Journal. A proactive Turn writes a Trace with the task proactive, the result proactive_message_sent or proactive_message_failed, the Budget, and the tokens spent before the Turn, and an Operator metric of the kind proactive_message with the Event id in blob5. An Outcome has an Operator metric of the kind outcome, with the result acted, replied, muted, or ignored and the Event id of the Proactive Message in blob5. A held Proactive Message has a Trace with the task proactive_hold, the result proactive_message_held, the Schedule id, the old and new due instant, and the reason, and no model fields.

The Channel send, reaction, and typing actions and the Telegram Channel: it decodes private text messages from Telegram updates, with the forward origin name (one line, at most 100 characters) of a forwarded message, and sends a plain-text message, split into parts within the Telegram limit of 4,096 characters. The send action takes an optional message to reply to; with none, the request has no reply parameters. A send is confirmed only with a Telegram message id. The reaction action (react) sets one emoji reaction on a message with Telegram setMessageReaction and is confirmed with Telegram ok. The Channel keeps the list of reactions that Telegram allows bots to use: allowedReaction drops variation selectors and skin tones and gives an allowed emoji, a close match from a small mapping, or nothing. The typing action (showTyping) sends Telegram sendChatAction with typing and fails with TypingNotShown when Telegram refuses it or cannot be reached; it is not a Delivery.

The typed Behavior Config defaults: the texting style, the tool step limit of a Turn, the size limit of the Profile in characters, and an optional default time zone that the Owner Preference overrides. proactiveDailyTokenBudget, proactiveResponseWindowMillis (24 hours), and the default quietHours (the Brief is at the end).
The branded Owner Id schema. Every Owner-scoped resource uses it as its key.

The control CLI of apps/agent: doctor checks configuration and secret names, dev runs the Worker locally with local fakes, owner add adds the Owner through the Operator route, request --contains proves a reply locally with no network (its fake model also sets the time zone and tells the local time), eval runs the Eval Cases against the real model (decision 0011), map writes and checks the Feature Map of the Edge routes, and bundle measures bundle size and local startup CPU.

The Eval runner. pnpm control eval runs each Eval Case k times against the real model through AI Gateway and reports pass^k, the failed checks, and the tokens of the agent and the judge. Each run uses a new Owner in the real Worker under the wrangler test harness, with temporary storage and a fake Telegram API. The eval Worker entry (apps/agent/eval) is the real Edge and Personal Agent plus seed, observation, and judge routes behind the Operator token; the deployed Worker does not include it. A case is a typed file in control/eval/cases, decoded by a schema before any model call: optional seeded Notes and Profile entries, Owner Events (text or forwarded), and checks. Code checks read Notes, links, the Profile, and the tool calls of the Trace; reply_judged uses the eval_judge Model Task with a fixed rubric.

The static marketing site: an Astro project whose home page shows Billy in his pixel valley, the chat (Bubble and Card contracts), the Brief, actions, privacy, self-hosting, and questions, plus a 404 page. It builds plain HTML and CSS from @repo/tokens and @repo/mascot, with shadcn/ui controls (Button, Accordion, Sheet) mapped to the tokens and hydrated as React islands only where needed. One script switches day and night from the sun or moon with a View Transition, and reveals sections on scroll; the scenery drifts and flows in CSS, and all motion stops under reduced motion.
